{{short description|American physicist}}
'''Vernon Willard Hughes''' (May 28, 1921 – March 25, 2003) was an American [[physicist]] specializing in research of subatomic particles.<ref name="NYT">[https://www.nytimes.com/2003/03/31/nyregion/dr-vernon-w-hughes-81-authority-on-the-subatomic.html?scp=1&sq=Vernon%20Willard%20Hughes&st=cse New York Times:Dr. Vernon W. Hughes, 81, Authority on the Subatomic, By STUART LAVIETES, Published: March 31, 2003]</ref><ref name="NN">[http://www.nndb.com/people/451/000169941/ NNDB:Vernon W. Hughes]</ref>
<ref name="NAP">[http://www.nap.edu/readingroom.php?book=biomems&page=vhughes.html National Academies Press:BIOGRAPHICAL MEMOIRS:Vernon Willard Hughes, By Robert K. Adair]</ref>
Hughes was born in [[Kankakee, Illinois]]. During World War II, he worked at the [[Radiation Laboratory|M.I.T. Radiation Lab]]. He earned his PhD under [[Isidor Isaac Rabi|I. I. Rabi]] at [[Columbia University]] in 1950.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Adair, Robert K.|authorlink=Robert Adair (physicist)|author2=Zeller, Michael E.|title=Obituary: Vernon Willard Hughes|journal=Physics Today|date=February 2004|volume=57|issue=2|pages=77–78|doi=10.1063/1.1688080|doi-access=free}}</ref> Hughes was notable for his research of [[muons]]<ref name="Hughes">
{{cite journal
 |author=V.W Hughes|year=1960
 | authorlink =Vernon W. Hughes 
 |title=Formation of Muonium and Observation of its Larmor Precession
 |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]]
 |volume=5 |issue=2 |pages=63&ndash;65
 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.5.63
|bibcode=1960PhRvL...5...63H
|display-authors=etal}}</ref> which showed the existence of previously undetected matter.<ref name="NYT"/>
He was also noted for research that showed that [[protons]] have [[gluons]] and [[quarks]].<ref name="NYT"/>
Hughes was a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]],<ref name="NN"/><ref name="NAP"/> [[Sterling Professor]] at [[Yale University]],<ref name="NYT"/><ref name="NAP"/> and a recipient of [[Rumford Prize]],<ref name="NN"/> and a recipient of [[Davisson–Germer Prize in Atomic or Surface Physics|Davisson-Germer Prize in Atomic Physics]] and  the [[Tom W. Bonner Prize in Nuclear Physics]], both from the [[American Physical Society]].<ref name="NAP"/>
